key_insight: Double-pulse resistance spot welding improves heat control and produces more consistent, stronger spot welds than conventional single-pulse RSW.
engineering_relevance: The process is especially relevant for automotive and structural manufacturing of advanced high-strength steels and dissimilar metal joints where weld quality and repeatability are critical.
method: Apply a pre-heating pulse to initiate nugget formation.
Use an inter-pulse cooling phase to reduce overheating and expulsion.
Finish with a high-current main pulse to complete a stable weld nugget.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes reported trends showing better temperature control, smaller heat-affected zones, higher tensile shear strength and failure energy, and more consistent nugget formation with DP-RSW.
watch_item: Implementation must still be tuned carefully, since performance depends on material pair, current waveform, and timing; poor parameter selection can negate the thermal benefits.
paper_title: A comprehensive review of Double-Pulse resistance spot welding for enhanced weld quality and mechanical performance
